brief: Goldman sales note aggregating desk views on five client questions plus systematic trade ideas. Rates: Sehgal runs short duration in the belly rather than the long end, paired with long risk assets, and does not expect a runaway selloff because CTAs have been short through the last 30bp and mortgage negative convexity is small, leaving issuance, sovereign wealth funds and Treasury buybacks as the drivers. Cole calls the selloff global, broad and low in volatility, so lower yields need a fundamentals change, most plausibly softer inflation, and relief comes at the front end. Gas: Dart's winter TTF range is 45 EUR/MWh if Hormuz LNG flows normalize and about 105 if they do not. Stehn maps a 100 EUR outcome to 0.6pp more headline and 0.3pp more core euro area inflation, while keeping next week's ECB move as the last hike of the cycle with a low hurdle for a third in December. Fed: September sits at 14.5bp priced, Brown expects a divided committee, Bingham argues the Fed hikes even on a 20bp core print. Japan: BoJ pricing has little hawkish room left and Cole sees 10y JGBs at 3% by year-end. EM positioning is light but entry levels are poor.
